content: With Rigify enabled, [k]Shift-A > Armature > Rigify Meta-Rigs > Basic > Basic Human[/k] and add to the scene (Image 1). If the metarig doesn't match the size of your mesh, scale it down and then [k]Ctrl-A,S[/k] to apply the scale, otherwise you will have problems later (Image 2).

image.caption: Image 1 - Enabling Rigify and adding a Basic Human Meta-Rig to the scene
Image 2 - Scaling the metarig down to match the size of the mesh and applying the scale to avoid problems later

content: You may need to make some fine adjustments to the metarig before parenting to your mesh. Select the metarig, go to Edit Mode, and enable symmetry across the x-axis (Image 3). Starting from the legs, begin aligning the metarig from the front (Image 4) and side (Image 5), focusing on these parts:

image.caption: Image 3 - Selecting the metarig, going to Edit Mode, and enabling symmetry across the x-axis
Image 4 - Starting from the legs and aligning the metarig from the front
Image 5 - Aligning the metarig from the side

content: Pay special attention to the heel bone. It needs to be at the back of the heel (Image 6) and as wide as the foot (Image 7).

image.caption: Image 6 - Positioning the heel bone at the back of the heel
Image 7 - Making the heel bone as wide as the foot

content: Rotate the arm bones in Edit Mode if needed, and align the shoulder, elbow, and wrist from the front (Image 8), and top (Image 9). Since the basic rig has no finger bones, move the hand bone past the first knuckle. Select the collarbone and [k]R,Z[/k] to straighten it out and then move it back in the y-axis to get it inside the mesh volume (Image 10). Move the breastbones out to where the breasts would be, or delete them (Image 11).

image.caption: Image 8 - Rotating the arm bones in Edit Mode with symmetry enabled and aligning the shoulder, elbow, and wrist from the front
Image 9 - Aligning the shoulder, elbow, and wrist from the side
Image 10 - Selecting the collarbone, rotating it in the z-axis to straighten it out and moving it back in the y-axis to get it inside the mesh volume
Image 11 - Moving the breastbones out to where the breasts would be or deleting them

content: Hide the leg and arm bones and them move the head parts of the hips and spine bones more towards the center of the body (Image 12).

image.caption: Image 12 - Hiding the leg and arm bones and moving the head parts of the hips and spine bones more towards the center of the body

content: When moving aligning bones along the spine, be careful not to accidentally separate them; if you do wou will get errors when you try to generate the rig. Align the two neck bones with the middle of the neck (Image 13) and the head bone with the top of the head and the back of the jaw below the ear (Image 14).

image.caption: Image 13 - Aligning the two neck bones with the middle of the neck
Image 14 - Aligning the head bone with the top of the head and the back of the jaw below the ear

content: [k]Alt-H[/k] to un-hide any bones and in the Data Properties tab click [k]Rigify > Generate Rig[/k] (Image 15). Then select the mesh and the new rig object that was created as the active object and [k]Ctrl-P > With Automatic Weights[/k].

image.caption: Image 15 - Un-hiding any bones and clicking Generate Rig in the Data Properties tab under Rigify

content: An important feature of Rigify is that you can keep tweaking the rig after generation. You can go back to Edit Mode, select the metarig and move your bones around if you didn't like their position. In the Data Properties tab you will see the option has changed to [k]Rigify > Re-Generate Rig[/k] (Image 16).

image.caption: Image 16 - Going back to Edit Mode on the metarig to adjust bone positions and seeing the option has changed to Re-Generate Rig in the Data Properties tab under Rigify

content: One of the most common problems you will have with Rigify has to do with the disconnected bones. Let's say you accidentally disconnected two bones (Image 17) that lead to either a deformed rig or an error with generating one. You can fix this by turning on Snap and setting the Snape Base to Vertex (Image 18). When you move a bone's head or tail it will try to snap to the closest bone you move it near (Image 19). Another option is to select the end you want to connect to and [k]Shift-S,T[/k] to move the cursor there, select the other end and [k]Shift-S,E[/k] to move the selection to the cursor.

image.caption: Image 17 - Showing accidentally disconnected bones that lead to a deformed rig or an error when generating
Image 18 - Turning on Snap and setting the Snap Base to Vertex to fix disconnected bones
Image 19 - Moving a bone's head or tail to snap it to the closest bone nearby

content: Select the rig and go into Pose Mode. By default, both arms and legs will be in IK mode, meaning you pose the arms and legs using the IK controls on the hands and feet (Image 20).

Select the red arrows along the thigh and [k]R,R[/k] to enable trackball-style rotation in order to rotate the knee (Image 21). You can also select the red arrows and go to the Rig Main Properties tab and enable Toggle Pole, which will display the IK Pole Target that you can use to rotate the knee (Image 22).

You can turn off IK for the arms by selecting the IK control on the hand and [k]Rig Main Properties > IK-FK (hand.L) > 1.0[/k] (Image 23). Now you can control the movement of the arm using the individual arm bones (Image 24).

The main torso control is the box around the hips which will move the whole torso (Image 25). A curved hips control which controls the character's butt (Image 26). A curved chest control that rotates the upper body (Image 27). There are also individual controls for the shoulders (Image 28), neck (Image 29), head (Image 30), and spine (Image 31). If you enable X-Ray Mode, inside the rig are spherical controls that allow you to bend the mesh for cartoony effects (Image 32).
